fine_lines.title: Win hands down vs play a blinder
fine_lines.explanation_ar: win hands down تعني أن تفوز بسهولة كبيرة. play a blinder تعني أن تقدّم أداءً ممتازاً جداً (قد تفوز أو لا).
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Win hands down' = win very easily. 'Play a blinder' = perform extremely well, whether you win or not (UK, informal).

examples.sentence: We won the quiz hands down.
Our goalkeeper played a blinder today.

fine_lines.title: Hard pass vs run for the hills
fine_lines.explanation_ar: hard pass رفض واضح وحاسم لاقتراح ما. run for the hills تعني الهرب أو الابتعاد بسرعة عن شيء مخيف أو غير مرغوب.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Hard pass' = a firm 'no' to a suggestion. 'Run for the hills' = escape quickly from something you want to avoid.

examples.sentence: Swimming in the cold sea? Hard pass.
When they asked for volunteers to clean, everyone ran for the hills.

expressions.meaning_en: (informal) a definite 'no' to an idea or offer
expressions.example: Waking up at 5 a.m. on a holiday? That's a hard pass from me.
You played a blinder in the presentation today!

expressions.meaning_en: a state of very high excitement or emotion
expressions.example: Excitement reached fever pitch before the final.
Their team is much stronger - they'll win hands down.

expressions.meaning_en: to understand the real situation and what it means for you
expressions.example: You know the score: no homework, no football.

expressions.meaning_en: to escape or avoid something quickly
expressions.example: When my uncle starts telling his long stories, I run for the hills!

expressions.meaning_en: very difficult or complicated thinking to solve a problem or explain something
expressions.example: It took a lot of mental gymnastics to understand the train timetable.
Maybe this photo will jog your memory.

grammar.title: Sport words used in everyday English
grammar.explanation_ar: كثير من كلمات الرياضة تُستخدم في الحياة اليومية بمعنى مجازي: pass (تمريرة) → hard pass (رفض)، score (النتيجة) → know the score (يفهم الوضع)، jog (يهرول) → jog your memory. افهم المعنى من السياق.
grammar.explanation_en: Many sport words get a new, non-literal meaning in everyday English: pass → hard pass (a firm no), score → know the score (understand the situation), jog → jog your memory. Use context to understand.
examples: This photo might jog your memory.
